Prop Firms Explained for Beginners

A prop firm, short for proprietary trading firm, is a company that funds traders who pass an evaluation. This guide explains the basics for beginners.

What is a prop firm?

A prop firm gives traders a funded account after they pass an evaluation. The trader and the firm share profits according to a profit split.

How the evaluation works

The evaluation has a profit target and drawdown rules. Pass it and you receive a funded account.

Is a funded account real money?

Most funded accounts are simulated, with the firm paying real payouts from its own revenue. Read the terms before you pay an evaluation fee.
